audit.evidence_policy: Static source findings are not runtime qualification. Local AIMock behavior is recorded by the execution audit when available.

latest_stable_snapshot.source: public npm and PyPI registry dist-tags/releases, read-only

source_evidence.detail: Browser rendering reads catalog status and replaces an unsupported snippet with a not-supported notice.
Markdown framework selection only searches bundled demos; it never reads catalog status.
Markdown then emits the selected demo region as code.
Shared guide selects the quarantined gen-ui-interrupt cell.
Shared guide selects the quarantined interrupt-headless cell.
Shared guide selects the quarantined shared-state-streaming cell.
Quarantines both interrupt feature IDs while retaining their demo entries.
Quarantines state streaming and both interrupt feature IDs while demo entries remain.
Quarantines state streaming and both interrupt feature IDs while demo entries remain.

defects.root_cause: The browser component treats the generated catalog as the availability authority, but the raw Markdown/LLM renderer only searches demo-content. A quarantined feature with source bundled therefore appears unavailable in HTML and as runnable code in Markdown; one without a local demo can fall through to another framework's code.
defects.impact: The public Markdown endpoint and llms-full feed can tell a reader to implement a feature the corresponding browser guide explicitly marks unsupported, and can attribute another framework's example to the selected framework.
defects.validation_needed: After repair, render each affected framework URL in HTML and .md/.mdx, asserting the same availability notice and that no fallback framework code is emitted. Run generator, shell-docs typecheck/build, route probe, and local AIMock qualification separately.

defects.feature: Google ADK display-only generative UI and in-chat HITL

source_evidence.detail: The supported display-only feature points to /generative-ui/your-components/display-only.
The supported in-chat HITL feature points to /generative-ui/your-components/interactive.
The ADK tree contains no matching override files; the root content tree also lacks those two paths.
Generated routes try root then framework override; with neither source present they render the not-available fallback when another framework owns the topic.
A local production shell-docs probe returned HTML 200 with title google-adk but MDX 404 for both advertised routes; no redirect occurred and no provider or hosted demo was used.

defects.root_cause: The Google ADK docs-link contract advertises two supported canonical routes but neither route has a root guide nor an ADK override. Other integrations supply overrides for the same feature families, so the framework-scoped resolver cannot serve ADK guidance.
defects.impact: Readers following either Google ADK feature link get an HTML 200 representation titled only google-adk while the corresponding public Markdown endpoint is a 404. Neither representation delivers the ADK-specific setup and source contract advertised for manifest-wired demos.
defects.validation_needed: Add or deliberately remap the source-of-truth guide routes, regenerate docs data, then assert meaningful HTML and 200 Markdown output for both /google-adk URLs with ADK-owned snippets. Run their isolated AIMock cells before claiming behavior qualification.

defects.area: canonical runnable examples and Markdown parity
defects.feature: interactive guides, Built-in Agent frontend tools, and Built-in Agent tool rendering

source_evidence.detail: The shared LangGraph guide embeds feature-viewer.copilotkit.ai, including when served to the TypeScript variant.
Strands and Built-in Agent interactive pages inline an IframeSwitcher to the external feature viewer.
The Built-in Agent authored frontend-tools guide inlines an external feature-viewer iframe.
The Built-in Agent authored tool-rendering guide inlines external viewer demo and code frames.
The component renders its supplied URLs as external iframes.
Raw Markdown only has a conversion path for InlineDemo and keeps other JSX tags verbatim, so IframeSwitcher has no equivalent source extraction.

defects.root_cause: Selected guide sources still use the legacy external Feature Viewer through IframeSwitcher instead of Showcase-owned InlineDemo/source regions. The raw Markdown renderer does not convert IframeSwitcher to a provenance-preserving source excerpt.
defects.impact: The browser presents an unqualified external demo/code source rather than the canonical Showcase cell, LangGraph TypeScript inherits a LangGraph viewer target, and Markdown/LLM readers receive JSX rather than runnable source.
defects.validation_needed: Replace the selected-guide viewer embeds with the matching Showcase cell and explicit source region where an LLM-readable excerpt is needed. Verify browser and Markdown output per affected framework, then run the corresponding isolated AIMock cells.

defects.feature: declarative Hashbrown and declarative JSON Render

source_evidence.detail: Each selected cell has guide_binding status not-applicable and no projected public route or source candidate.
The active feature definitions omit canonical shell_docs_path values for these two feature IDs.
A real guide source already exists and declares the Hashbrown demo cell.
A real guide source already exists and declares the JSON Render demo cell.

defects.root_cause: The public guides and wired demos exist, but their active feature definitions omit the catalog docs contract. Inventory generation therefore cannot bind the ten selected cells to those existing guides or project a feature URL.
defects.impact: Readers can reach the pages through navigation but the feature catalog, showcase matrix, and feature-specific documentation links cannot discover or validate them as the guides for the wired feature IDs.
defects.validation_needed: Add canonical shell_docs_path values that point to the existing guides, regenerate the inventory, and validate the generated feature links and selected framework HTML/Markdown routes.

defects.area: native setup contract and HTML/Markdown parity
defects.feature: FrameworkSetup concepts referenced by selected wired/stub feature guides

no_additional_package_owned_setup.contexts: All five A2UI cells; all fourteen tool-rendering cells; four headless cells; two in-chat HITL cells; two subagent cells; both gen-ui-agent cells; and Built-in Agent readonly context. Their routed guides already provide the necessary selected source region or the runtime supplies the transport automatically.

conditionally_not_rendered.contexts: react/built-in-agent/agent-config: agent-config-setup is inside the shared-state branch, while this integration declares runtime-properties.

missing_native_setup_guidance.contexts: react/strands/shared-state-read-write, react/strands/readonly-state-agent-context, and react/strands/agent-config. These are promoted to CONTENT-GEN-009.

behavior_candidate.contexts: react/strands/shared-state-read. The UI writes recipe state but the adapter's explicit prompt lifter omits it; it remains CONTENT-GEN-008 pending local behavior evidence.

source_evidence.detail: The setup-content build contract loads package-owned concepts only from integrations/<slug>/docs/setup/<concept>.mdx (or the separate docs-only source).
Browser FrameworkSetup resolves the generated setup bundle and returns null when the selected framework/concept pair is absent.
Markdown resolves the same bundle but emits a setup-skipped HTML comment for every absent concept except channels-agent-setup.
The selected A2UI guide requests a2ui-fixed-schema-setup, but no selected integration owns that setup fragment.
The selected tool-rendering guide requests tool-rendering-setup, but LangGraph Python, LangGraph TypeScript, ADK, and Strands do not own that setup fragment.

defects.root_cause: Thirty-five selected wired/stub cells resolve MDX that requests a package-owned FrameworkSetup concept unavailable for that integration. Browser rendering silently removes the block while Markdown emits a skipped-setup comment. Semantic review classified thirty as intentional/redundant because the guide already exposes the selected implementation or the runtime supplies the transport, one as a branch that does not render, three as genuine Strands native-setup omissions, and one as an adapter-behavior candidate.
defects.impact: The cross-surface structural mismatch remains observable, but the raw count must not be interpreted as thirty-five missing backend steps. The three confirmed Strands omissions and one behavior candidate are tracked separately to keep the planned reader guidance minimal.
defects.validation_needed: Regenerate setup-content and render HTML and Markdown after any repair. Ensure the three required Strands backend adapters get reader-visible native setup, while intentionally redundant setup is either omitted consistently or marked as covered by the routed source. Run isolated AIMock cells separately.

source_evidence.detail: The selected transitive snippet says a catch-all applies when no specific useRenderToolCall is defined.
The explanatory callout says useRenderToolCall targets a specific tool by name.
The current v2 hook is a consumer that returns a renderer function; it does not register a named renderer.
The current v2 named-renderer registration API is useRenderTool.
The repository's current API reference explicitly warns that v2 useRenderToolCall has different semantics from the v1 registration hook.

defects.root_cause: A shared guide snippet retains the v1 meaning of useRenderToolCall while its code and linked reference otherwise present v2 APIs.
defects.impact: Built-in Agent readers are told the wrong hook supplies a named renderer, making the current API reference and feature guide contradict one another.
defects.validation_needed: Describe named registration with useRenderTool and reserve useRenderToolCall for rendering/consuming existing tool calls. Verify the selected Built-in Agent guide's browser and Markdown output against the v2 reference.

defects.area: runnable example and native runtime-properties guidance

source_evidence.detail: The integration declares runtime-properties, so its feature guide selects the in-process provider-properties contract.
The selected runtime-properties guide tells React readers to pass config through CopilotKit properties; it documents input.forwardedProps as the factory input.
The featured demo provider sets a runtime URL and agent but does not pass properties; it instead mounts ConfigContextRelay.
The relay publishes preferences with useAgentContext, a different input channel.
The dedicated in-process factory reads only input.forwardedProps before it builds the configuration prompt.

defects.root_cause: A LangGraph-oriented context relay was reused in the Built-in Agent demo even though the Built-in Agent route consumes provider properties. The page comments also describe a Python middleware that does not exist in this in-process runtime.
defects.impact: Isolated local browser request capture confirms that changed controls are serialized in protocol context while forwardedProps is empty. The featured factory reads only forwardedProps, so it builds its default configuration prompt despite the control changes.
defects.validation_needed: Repair the channel mismatch, then add a neutral-message regression assertion that changed controls appear in forwardedProps consumed by the factory. The existing D6 response-difference fixture is not sufficient because it selects replies by userMessage.

d6_assessment.evidence: An isolated Next server at 127.0.0.1:3127 and a temporary Playwright interceptor captured agent/run before the route handler or AIMock. With three changed controls and a neutral sentinel message, context held the values and forwardedProps was {}.

source_evidence.detail: The UI seeds and updates agent.state.recipe and presents the feature as agent-readable recipe state.
The manifest promises that the neutral agent reads the recipe context without mutating it.
The explicit state_context_builder documents the state slots it injects and accepts input state.
That builder injects preferences and todos only; it has no recipe branch.
The Strands agent registers that builder as its state_context_builder.

defects.root_cause: The showcased state key and the adapter's documented prompt-lifting allowlist diverge. Static inspection cannot rule out an unobserved adapter-level state injection, so this remains a behavior candidate.
defects.impact: Audit-only direct execution of the registered state_context_builder confirms that a unique recipe sentinel is omitted from the constructed prompt, while a preferences control sentinel is retained. The promised recipe is therefore absent from the explicit state-to-model bridge.
defects.validation_needed: Add recipe serialization to the state bridge and a sentinel regression test. The existing D6 reply assertion is not sufficient because its fixture matches userMessage and returns recipe terms without inspecting state.

d6_assessment.evidence: The unchanged build_state_prompt was invoked with recipe.title=AUDIT_RECIPE_SENTINEL_7f3c9a and omitted it, while preferences.name=AUDIT_PREFERENCE_SENTINEL_7f3c9a was retained. This is bridge-scope execution, not a full transport capture.

defects.feature: Strands state context and agent configuration

source_evidence.detail: The shared-state guide requests native shared-state-setup before promising UI writes steer the agent.
The read-only-context guide requests agent-context-setup before saying backend context injection reaches the model.
The shared-state agent-config branch requests agent-config-setup and says the selected setup shows the backend bridge.
Strands owns only frontend-tools and channels setup fragments; none of the three requested native setup concepts is bundled.
The adapter needs a custom context formatter because ag_ui_strands does not otherwise surface context to the model.
The same custom prompt builder lifts state values before model invocation.
StrandsAgentConfig installs that state_context_builder for the runnable agent.

defects.root_cause: The Strands implementation needs an adapter-specific state/context prompt bridge, but its package supplies no setup fragments for the three guides that claim or require that bridge. Browser docs omit the setup entirely and Markdown reports it skipped.
defects.impact: A reader copying the generic React state/context calls has no Strands-native instruction for getting those values into the model, despite these cells relying on custom prompt lifting.
defects.validation_needed: Add concise Strands setup fragments that expose the existing state_context_builder pattern for each relevant concept, regenerate setup content, and verify HTML and Markdown show matching native guidance. Re-run the three isolated cells with AIMock.

source_evidence.detail: Built-in Agent declares a2ui_pattern schema-inline, which selects the inline-schema branch of the shared guide.
The reader-facing delivery taxonomy names only Spring AI and .NET for schema-inline, omitting the selected Built-in Agent despite its schema-inline manifest contract.
The selected schema-inline branch requests backend-schema-json-load.
That selected branch renders the requested backend-schema-json-load snippet.
The Built-in Agent fixed-schema implementation has no backend-schema-json-load region to satisfy the guide request.

The expanded local production response audit found the scoped HTML route emits a Missing snippet alert for built-in-agent::a2ui-fixed-schema/backend-schema-json-load; both final representations were otherwise 200.

defects.root_cause: The generic schema-inline A2UI guide assumes each selected integration publishes a backend-schema-json-load region and its delivery taxonomy does not account for Built-in Agent. Built-in Agent uses a different fixed-schema implementation but does not supply a compatible region or a framework override.
defects.impact: The supported Built-in Agent A2UI guide visibly reports a missing source excerpt instead of presenting a copyable native implementation, while its opening classification also leaves readers without a stated Built-in Agent path. The Markdown route succeeds, so representation status alone masks the documentation failure.
defects.validation_needed: Add a Built-in-Agent-appropriate region or a scoped guide branch that describes its actual fixed-schema factory, then assert no Missing snippet alert and useful HTML/Markdown source for the scoped route. Run its isolated AIMock cell separately.

source_evidence.detail: The overview sentence contains the malformed phrase 'utilized for to let', obscuring the three stated use cases.
The walkthrough introduces 'a approval flow' rather than an approval flow.

defects.root_cause: The shared LangGraph interactive guide has unedited prose in the reader-facing introduction and setup transition.
defects.impact: The guide is still understandable, but the first explanation for this supported feature reads as unfinished and weakens the intended human-friendly documentation standard.
defects.validation_needed: Edit the two sentences and confirm the LangGraph Python and TypeScript HTML/Markdown pages retain their shared source and feature routing.

defects.feature: Google ADK and AWS Strands quickstarts

source_evidence.detail: The v2 quickstart installs @copilotkit/react-ui alongside react-core, runtime, and ag-ui/client.
Its provider example imports CopilotKit and styles only from @copilotkit/react-core/v2.
The v2 Strands quickstart repeats the @copilotkit/react-ui installation.
Its provider and stylesheet imports also use @copilotkit/react-core/v2 only.
The parallel current v2 quickstart explicitly states that @copilotkit/react-ui is not needed when using CopilotKit and CopilotSidebar from react-core/v2.

defects.root_cause: The ADK and Strands install instructions include @copilotkit/react-ui even though the displayed current v2 provider, component, and stylesheet imports use react-core/v2 only.
defects.impact: Readers follow an avoidable package-install step before using the selected feature-guide dependencies. This is a documentation-minimality issue only; the audit does not claim the package itself is nonworking or unsupported.
defects.validation_needed: When the adjacent setup instructions are next changed, remove @copilotkit/react-ui if no omitted step requires it, retain the required runtime and AG-UI client packages, then run the scoped quickstart doctests/build and confirm the generated instructions in HTML and Markdown.

source_evidence.detail: The integration defines the exact /api/copilotkit-auth App Router endpoint.
The same integration also defines an optional catch-all endpoint under the identical base path.
The manifest binds the root auth route into the auth demo, so the conflicting route tree is part of the committed Showcase integration.

local_execution_evidence.environment: Baseline source, Node v22.16.0, installed Next 15.5.19; no hosted service, provider key, or source modification used.
local_execution_evidence.result: The process exited before listening because Next rejects equally specific routes /api/copilotkit-auth and /api/copilotkit-auth[[...slug]]. The agent service at port 8001 was independently healthy.
local_execution_evidence.provenance: Observed by the local feature audit on the unchanged baseline; its Google ADK host-runtime report is pending.

defects.root_cause: Next App Router cannot register an exact route and an optional catch-all route with the same base-path specificity. Both are committed beneath the Google ADK frontend API tree.
defects.impact: The Google ADK frontend cannot start locally, so every Google ADK Showcase demo and corresponding guide that promises a runnable local example is unavailable before the page-specific feature behavior can be exercised. This is an observed launch failure, distinct from the source-only mismatch in CONTENT-GEN-007.
defects.validation_needed: Keep one unambiguous auth route shape, start the Google ADK frontend against the local agent, then run the manifest-wired cells with the local AIMock harness and recheck the affected guide routes.

source_evidence.detail: The LangSmith sample says thread identity makes histories per-user, then derives that identity directly from x-user-id and x-user-name request headers.
The FastAPI sample repeats the same client-controlled identity derivation.
The ADK quickstart repeats the same per-user claim and derives identifyUser directly from x-user-id and x-user-name request headers.
The Strands quickstart repeats the same per-user claim and derives identifyUser directly from x-user-id and x-user-name request headers.
The canonical Intelligence runtime guide repeats the same client-controlled header derivation while saying it scopes threads per user.
The shared authentication guide demonstrates resolving identity from a server-verified session before identifyUser returns it.
The same guide requires an ownership guard for Intelligence routes that are not platform user-scoped.

defects.root_cause: The quickstarts use client-supplied headers as an identity shortcut while presenting the result as per-user thread isolation. They neither mark the shortcut as single-user/local-only nor supply server-side authentication and the required guards for unscoped routes.
defects.impact: A reader who deploys these samples without an independent upstream identity guard allows a client to choose a user id and thus receives no actual per-user isolation from the shown callback. The guides make this unsafe interpretation likely by presenting it as the isolation mechanism.
defects.validation_needed: Replace the header shortcut with a server-verified session example (or state it is strictly local single-user), add the required onRequest and ownership guards or link to the exact complete auth setup, then verify all four affected quickstart representations and a two-user local authorization probe.

source_evidence.detail: The starter troubleshooting tells a reader to try 0.0.0.0 instead of localhost for a connection.
The example correctly uses localhost as the server bind host and the runtime target is localhost:8000.
The bring-your-own troubleshooting repeats 0.0.0.0 as a suggested client connection target.
The Strands quickstart also recommends 0.0.0.0 as a replacement for a localhost client target.
The Built-in Agent quickstart likewise recommends 0.0.0.0 as a replacement for a localhost client target.

defects.root_cause: The guide confuses a wildcard server bind address with an address a client should connect to.
defects.impact: The troubleshooting advice is nonportable: 0.0.0.0 denotes a server wildcard bind, not a portable client destination. It can send readers away from valid loopback URLs without the audit claiming an observed connection failure.
defects.validation_needed: Remove 0.0.0.0 as a client target, explain it only as an optional server bind address if needed, retain valid loopback targets, then recheck both starter and bring-your-own rendered troubleshooting sections.

source_evidence.detail: The Rich Threads overview embeds a hand-written tracked coding-agent prompt with its own init command, cloud-hosted assumptions, and verification procedure.
The existing canonical Rich Threads prompt delegates to the add-rich-threads CLI intent.
The shared prompt factory says feature cards must not repeat setup instructions because the CLI intent owns links, planning, prerequisite refusal, and proof.

defects.root_cause: The Threads overview predates or bypasses the shared RichThreadsSetupPrompt contract and duplicates a setup flow in page content.
defects.impact: The public overview has a second Rich Threads coding-agent flow whose assumptions and verification language can drift from the CLI-owned add-rich-threads route. This conflicts with the requirement to reuse the existing helper rather than create another prompt contract.
defects.validation_needed: Replace the embedded hand-written handoff with RichThreadsSetupPrompt (or a wrapper that passes through its exact prompt), preserve only page-specific context outside the copied prompt, then assert browser and raw Markdown expose the same canonical command and that the CLI intent remains the source of setup steps.

defects.area: local runnable Showcase default development command
affected_contexts: react/langgraph-typescript/all active demo and feature-guide cells under the checked-in default dev command

source_evidence.detail: The checked-in dev script launches Next with --turbopack.
The NodeNext .js-to-.ts/.tsx/.js resolver compatibility is configured only in the webpack callback.
The staged emitter imports its co-located TypeScript leaves through explicit .js specifiers.
The main API route imports the CVDIAG wrapper, so normal demo requests compile through the incompatible importer.
Local host evidence records the default Turbopack API-route overlay/500 and a healthy unchanged-source Webpack-mode control run.

defects.root_cause: The default command selects Turbopack, but only the webpack configuration supplies the extension alias needed for NodeNext-style .js imports to co-located .ts CVDIAG leaves.
defects.impact: The UI can initially load, then normal API route compilation overlays and returns 500. The first 18 LangGraph TypeScript D6 attempts launched this way are not valid behavior qualification, rather than passing or failing feature evidence.
defects.validation_needed: Make the checked-in default development command and resolver configuration compatible, then run the complete LangGraph TypeScript D6 matrix from a fresh local service. The observed unchanged-source Webpack control command served /api/health and /demos/agentic-chat with 200 but is not a repair.
